As enlarge person: each humanoid doubles in height, multiplies its weight by 8 and rises one size category, gaining the space and reach of that size, with equipment enlarged alongside it and speed unchanged.

enlarge-person-mass.notes: Description is only 'functions like enlarge person, except that it affects multiple creatures'; every number was read from enlarge person's own description in this corpus. Affects one humanoid per caster level, none more than 30 feet apart.

effects.target: attack rolls made with your tail or tail weapons
damage rolls made with your tail or tail weapons
Your tail gains 5 feet of reach when you attack with it or with tail weapons.

enlarge-tail.notes: Both bonuses apply only to tail attacks, so they are situational_mods — combat_mods would improve every attack the caster makes. Neither has a stated bonus type. Reach has no effect type; `speed` covers movement modes, not the distance a creature threatens.

effects.target: An hour of careful regulation of your body's energies makes your steps lighter than air, granting you the benefits of air walk.
At any time you may expend the spell's entire remaining duration as a swift action to gain a fly speed of 120 feet with perfect manoeuvrability for 1 minute, after which the spell ends.

enlightened-step.notes: The fly 120 ft. is stated, but it is not emitted as a `speed` spec: it exists only after the caster spends a swift action to burn the rest of the spell, and a speed spec would grant it from the moment of casting. Corpus duration is 'hours (24) or until discharged'; the discharge is the swift-action trade recorded above.

effects.target: You are warded against mental prying — divinations such as detect thoughts and seek thoughts, and enchantments such as modify memory and memory lapse. A creature targeting you with any mind-affecting spell that detects or alters your thoughts or memories must succeed at a caster level check against DC 11 + your caster level or the spell fails. Only thought- and memory-reaching effects are blocked; clairaudience/clairvoyance, detect evil, locate creature and the like affect you normally.

enshroud-thoughts.notes: Not an `immunity`: the ward is a caster level check the other caster may beat, not a refusal, and the engine's immunity path does not consult a DC.

effects.target: ref

on_failure.target: entangled

effects.target: Plants in a 40-foot-radius spread wrap around creatures in the area. A creature that saves may move normally, but must save again at the end of your turn if it stays; a creature entering the area saves immediately, and on a failure must end its movement and become entangled. An entangled creature may try to break free as a move action with a Strength or Escape Artist check against the spell's DC. The whole area is difficult terrain for the duration. If the plants are thorny, a creature takes 1 point of damage each time it fails a save against the entangle or fails a check to break free, and the GM may allow other effects depending on the local plants.

entangle.notes: The 1 point of thorn damage is NOT a damage spec. It is conditional on the local plants being thorny, which the spell leaves to the GM, and it recurs on every failed save or escape check for as long as the spell lasts — the vocabulary has no repeating or conditional damage.

effects.target: You gain a dim awareness of what happens around every object bearing your face or form within range, whether one or thousands: each has the full range of your senses and you may attempt Perception checks through it, always at DC 10 higher than if you were there yourself. You may fill one such image with your consciousness at a time, which blinds you to the others while leaving you aware of your own body's surroundings; your body is defenceless and helpless, automatically failing every saving throw, and you can return to it at any moment as an immediate action.

An occupied image gains limited animation: statues and other three-dimensional likenesses can turn their heads, gesture and speak but cannot attack or leave their square unaided, while portraits can speak and move anywhere within the picture or briefly alter it. You cannot use spells or other abilities from inside an image. Leaving it returns you to your body and the object reverts to its former appearance at once. If the image is damaged or destroyed you return to your body unharmed. The spell ends when you stop concentrating, if dispel magic is cast on the image or on your body, or if your body is killed.

enter-image.notes: Projecting consciousness has no effect type. The caster's helplessness is a cost of the projection he chooses to incur and can end as an immediate action, so it is not an apply_condition.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Speaking or singing without interruption for 1 full round holds an audience: those affected give you their undivided attention, ignore their surroundings, and are treated as having a friendly attitude. They take no action while you perform and for 1d3 rounds afterward while they discuss it. A target with 4 or more Hit Dice or Wisdom 16 or higher instead stays aware of its surroundings, is only indifferent, and gains a new save if it sees you do something it opposes. Creatures entering the area during the performance must also save or be enthralled. A creature of a race or religion unfriendly to yours gains +4 on its save.

effects.target: The effect lasts only as long as you speak or sing, to a maximum of 1 hour, and ends — though the 1d3-round delay still applies — if you lose concentration or do anything but perform. Unfriendly or hostile listeners who were not enthralled may collectively heckle you, making one Charisma check using the highest Charisma in the group with others assisting; beating your own Charisma check ends the spell, and only one such challenge is allowed per casting. If any listener is attacked or subjected to an overtly hostile act the spell ends and the formerly enthralled become unfriendly toward you — hostile, for those with 4 or more Hit Dice or Wisdom 16 or higher.

enthrall.notes: 'Enthralled' is not a 1e condition and the text never names fascinated, so no apply_condition was emitted — the effect is described in the words the spell uses. The +4 for an unfriendly race or religion is a bonus on the save that gates this spell and is conditional on the listener's own race and faith, so it is not a save_mod. The attitude change is not in the vocabulary either.

effects.target: As lesser entice fey, except the calling can produce a single fey of 12 Hit Dice or fewer, or two fey of the same kind whose Hit Dice total no more than 12, appearing no more than 30 feet apart.

entice-fey.notes: Calling a creature has no effect type. The Hit Dice are a limit on what answers, not dice to roll.

effects.target: As lesser entice fey, except the calling can produce a single fey of 18 Hit Dice or fewer, or up to three fey of the same kind whose Hit Dice total no more than 18, appearing no more than 30 feet apart.

entice-fey-greater.notes: Calling a creature has no effect type.

effects.target: As lesser planar ally, except that you entice a fey of 6 Hit Dice or fewer with an offering of music or something else it finds appealing. Which fey answers is up to the whims of nature and the fey, not your choice. Besides the material component you must succeed at a Knowledge (nature) or Perform check against DC 20 + the target's Hit Dice, and the highest Hit Dice you can call this casting equals your check result minus 20 — a high result never exceeds the spell's own cap, and a result of 20 or less calls nothing. Once it appears you negotiate for its service and your payment; if it dislikes your offer it may simply refuse, and you expend neither the offerings nor the payment.

entice-fey-lesser.notes: The 'check result of 24 means 4 Hit Dice' passage is a worked example and none of its numbers are rules.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target is filled with a deep desire to protect and care for you, fawning over your needs and comfort.

Whenever another creature harms you, the target is overcome with rage and compelled to attack the aggressor, gaining a +2 morale bonus to Strength and Constitution, a +1 morale bonus on Will saves, and a -2 penalty to Armour Class. The rage lasts until the instigator is defeated or retreats, or the target is killed or knocked unconscious; if several creatures have harmed you it continues until all are beaten or driven off, after which the target is fatigued for as many rounds as it raged. It rages again each time you are harmed, but cannot rage while fatigued. If you are reduced below 0 hit points, the target must succeed at a second Will save or be compelled to defend your body, attacking anyone who approaches, for the rest of the duration — and if it succeeds at that save the spell ends immediately.

enticing-adulation.notes: The four rage modifiers are stated with their bonus types, but they are deliberately left narrative: they exist only while the target is raging, which starts when a third party harms the caster and stops when that creature is beaten. Emitting them as ability_mod, save_mod and combat_mod would give the target +2 Strength, +2 Constitution and -2 AC from the moment of casting and never take them away. Fatigued is not emitted for the same reason — it follows the rage ending, not the casting.

effects.target: You send an aboveground area of up to three 10-foot cubes per caster level deep underground, with minor tremors during the casting warning anyone nearby. The area and every creature in it at the end of the casting are sealed in a self-contained vault whose highest point lies up to 10 feet per caster level below the surface. The vault's magic preserves the natural light, temperature and air quality the area had aboveground — a sunny field stays brightly lit indefinitely — but does not extend the duration of magical effects, so a daylight spell still expires on time. You may leave a tunnel to the surface up to 20 feet wide or seal the vault off entirely. Nothing already in the ground is destroyed; it is pushed further down, and if the spell is dispelled the area returns to the surface and everything displaced returns with it, the vault pushing harmlessly aside anything now standing in its way.

entomb.notes: Burying a volume of terrain has no effect type. Nobody takes damage — the spell never states any, and the displaced earth is explicitly not destructive.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The incorporeal creature or haunt is trapped inside the mirror that is the spell's focus and cannot be affected by any means while inside it. If the mirror is destroyed, a trapped incorporeal creature is freed at once and a trapped haunt returns to its original location. A creature that became incorporeal through a spell or other means stays incorporeal while trapped, even if that effect's own duration runs out.

entrap-spirit.notes: If the focus mirror belonged to the target, the target takes -2 on this saving throw. Not emitted as a save_mod: it is a penalty on the gating save itself, conditional on who owned the focus, and a spec would attach a standing -2 Will to the victim instead.

effects.target: A field of chaotic multicoloured light surrounds you and deflects incoming arrows, rays and other ranged attacks: every ranged attack against you that requires an attack roll has a 20% miss chance, as concealment. Attacks that simply work at a distance without an attack roll are unaffected.

entropic-shield.notes: Same gap as displacement: the vocabulary has no miss-chance or concealment effect, and this is the whole of the spell. It is not a combat_mod to AC — a miss chance is rolled after a hit is already established, so writing it as +AC would change which attacks land.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Seething envy turns each affected creature on the nearest creature, ally or enemy alike, to attempt one of the following at your choice: disarm it of a valuable weapon, steal something it is holding, or grapple it and strip it of something it prizes. An affected creature may attempt a new Will save each round as a free action to end the effect.

envious-urge.notes: A compulsion to take a specific action is not a 1e condition — it is not confused, which has its own random behaviour table — so nothing in the condition vocabulary fits.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target contracts one disease of your choice — blinding sickness, bubonic plague, cackle fever, filth fever, leprosy, mindfire, red ache, shakes or slimy doom — as contagion. Here it is highly contagious: anyone who touches the target, is touched by it, or spends more than an hour in a confined space with it must save against the disease's own normal DC, not this spell's, or catch it too. If the original target throws off the disease by making the required saves, it stays a carrier for a time equal to the disease's frequency and can keep infecting others.

epidemic.notes: Disease is not in the condition vocabulary and each of the nine has its own DC, onset, frequency and ability damage track, none of which is reproduced here. Which disease is inflicted is the caster's choice, so even a single narrative cannot be narrowed further. No ability damage is emitted: it belongs to whichever disease is chosen and lands on later saves, not on casting.

effects.target: Removes magical or mundane writing from a scroll, or from one or two pages of paper, parchment or similar. It can remove explosive runes, a glyph of warding, a sepia snake sigil or an arcane mark, but not illusory script or a symbol spell. Nonmagical writing is erased automatically if you touch it and nobody else is holding it, and otherwise has a 90% chance of being erased. Magical writing must be touched and also needs a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against DC 15, on which a natural 1 always fails.

erase.notes: Failing to erase explosive runes, a glyph of warding or a sepia snake sigil sets that writing off instead. That is a failure consequence belonging to the triggered writing, not damage this spell deals, and this spell states no dice for it — so nothing was converted from it.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Banishes psychic impressions from the object touched, leaving it without recent history. You choose how much time to erase, up to 1 day per caster level, but always working backward from the present — you cannot leave recent events untouched. What is erased cannot be recovered by object reading, legend lore or similar means. Cast on a corpse it also strips recent impressions from while the creature was alive, putting those memories beyond speak with dead.

erase-impressions.notes: The 5th-level caster and the 2-day-old corpse are a worked example; none of those numbers are rules. The corpus's save is 'Will negates (object)', so the gate is kept even though the target is an object.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target loses 1 point from any damage reduction it has and 1 point from any natural armour bonus it has. Having failed the first save it may try again each round for the duration; failing again costs it another point of each, cumulatively. The first success stops the erosion, but every point already lost stays gone until the spell ends, at which point its damage reduction and natural armour return to normal at once. Only one erode defenses can affect a creature at a time.

erode-defenses.notes: Not typed for three reasons at once. The loss is cumulative, repeating once per round for as long as saves keep failing, and the vocabulary has no repeating effect. `damage_reduction` grants DR rather than subtracting it, and there is no negative form. And the amount removed is capped by whatever DR and natural armour the target already has, which no spec can read.

effects.target: Your skin erupts in swollen, pus-filled bumps that burst when you are struck. Any creature that hits you with its body or a hand-held weapon deals its damage normally, but at the same moment the attacker takes 1d6 points of acid damage and must make a Fortitude save or be sickened for 1 round — nauseated instead, on a failed save, if the attack was a critical hit. This acid damage can harm a swarm.

eruptive-pustules.notes: REFUSED TO CONVERT as damage. This is retributive damage — precisely the Thorn Body defect named in the brief. The spell's range is personal and its target is you; the 1d6 acid and the sickened/nauseated land on whoever strikes you, and only on the round they strike. A damage spec or an apply_condition here would burn and sicken the caster the moment the spell was cast, and would fire once instead of on every incoming attack.

effects.target: Wards ten 10-foot cubes per caster level and notifies you when a creature leaves the area, functioning as alarm otherwise. There is no password: instead you may attune up to one additional creature per caster level when you place it, and you are attuned automatically without counting against that limit. Attuned creatures come and go without triggering it. If you choose a mental alarm rather than an audible one, every attuned creature receives the mental alert when someone exits the warded area.

escape-alarm.notes: A ward that reports an event has no effect type and touches no creature's statistics.

effects.target: When a creature at least one size category larger than you attacks you and misses, you may move up to 5 feet away from it as an immediate action, without provoking attacks of opportunity. The distance rises by 5 feet for every 5 caster levels.

escaping-ward.notes: Not a `speed` spec: this is a reactive 5-foot reposition granted on a specific trigger, not an increase to any movement rate, and a speed spec would add 5 feet to the caster's walking every round instead.

effects.target: Cast as an immediate action after you are targeted by an attack or effect but before you learn its result: you step into the Ethereal Plane as ethereal jaunt, becoming ethereal until the beginning of your next turn, which dodges the blow or confounds the spell. On the turn after you return to your starting point you may take only move actions and free actions.

ether-step.notes: Duration omitted: the corpus says 'see text', and the text sets it by a turn boundary — 'until the beginning of your next turn' — which the shared format has no kind for. It is stated in the effect instead of being rounded to 1 round.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target is shunted to the Ethereal Plane and sealed in a cocoon of misty ethereal fibres, forced into a cataleptic meditative state as though unconscious. At the end of each of its turns it may attempt a Will save to wake itself. Once awake it counts as pinned, using your caster level as the cocoon's CMB and 10 + your caster level + your primary spellcasting ability modifier as its CMD. A successful grapple check or Escape Artist check downgrades pinned to grappled but does not free it, though it may attack the cocoon as described under ethereal envelope. If it breaks free, or you dismiss the spell, it returns to its previous location on the Material Plane — and if it is conscious at that moment it does not spend the usual round asleep or staggered.

ethereal-envelopment.notes: Pinned and grappled are both in the vocabulary but neither is emitted, because the target passes through a sequence of states — unconscious-like, then pinned once it wakes itself, then possibly grappled — driven by its own saves and checks each round. apply_condition has no way to order states or to hand one off to another, so emitting pinned would assert the wrong state for the first several rounds.

effects.target: Your hands reach into the Ethereal and Material planes at once, letting you deal normal damage to ethereal creatures with claws, unarmed strikes, and touch spells or effects. Miss chance from etherealness, such as the blink spell, does not apply against you, though miss chance from concealment still does.

ethereal-fists.notes: The spell adds no damage of its own — it only makes the caster's existing attacks able to connect with ethereal targets, so there is nothing to put in a damage spec.

effects.target: As ethereal jaunt, except that you and other willing creatures joined by linked hands become ethereal along with their equipment. Besides yourself you may bring one creature per 3 caster levels. Once ethereal the subjects need not stay together, and when the spell expires every affected creature still on the Ethereal Plane returns to material existence.

etherealness.notes: Planar travel has no effect type.

effects.target: Ethereal substance hardens into transdimensional razors, invisible to normal sight, filling one 10-foot cube per caster level. Movement through the area is halved, even for incorporeal creatures. A creature entering a 5-foot cube of shards takes 1d8 points of piercing and slashing damage and must succeed at a Reflex save or take 1 point of bleed damage, which stacks with itself and with other sources of bleed.

A creature standing in the area takes no damage while completely motionless, but even the small movements of attacking or defending force it to attempt a Reflex save: success avoids all damage that round, failure deals the hit point and bleed damage as though it had moved through the square. A creature forcibly moved through the shards, as by a bull rush or drag, takes -4 on that save, while a creature that can see invisible or ethereal objects gains +4 and takes no damage at all on a success. The shards count as a magical trap that a creature with trapfinding can locate by Perception at DC 25 + the spell's level, and they cannot be disabled with Disable Device.

etheric-shards.notes: The 1d8 and the 1 point of bleed are NOT emitted, though both are stated plainly. Nobody takes them when the spell is cast: this is a lingering hazard with an area and no creature target, and the damage fires whenever some creature later enters a 5-foot cube or moves while standing in one — repeatedly, for hours. A damage or bleed spec would hit the caster once at casting and never fire again, which is wrong in both directions. Two smaller gaps: the damage is 'piercing and slashing' together and damage_type holds one value, and `bleed` cannot be gated on a per-entry Reflex save.
